claims.evidence: RequestBuilder::send (the only send path) now calls toolkit_trace_context::inject_request_id for every request built by any HttpClient. toolkit-http is also the transport for external calls: toolkit-auth OAuth2 token fetch / OIDC discovery (libs/toolkit-auth/src/oauth2/fetch.rs, source.rs:127), and the OAGW oauth2 client-credentials plugin, which runs inline in DataPlaneServiceImpl::proxy_request (service.rs:697 -> 1271 -> oauth2_client_cred_auth.rs:214) within the gateway's with_request_id scope. OAGW's upstream header policy defaults to PassthroughMode::None (headers.rs:28), yet the token request to the IdP now carries the inbound id. HttpClientConfig has no knob and no preset (token_endpoint(), proxy) disables it.
claims.fix: Make forwarding opt-in per client (e.g. an HttpClientConfig flag enabled by the toolkit-contract client/proxy presets), or perform the injection in toolkit-contract's send_unary/send_open_request where the builder is still in the caller task, leaving the generic RequestBuilder::send unchanged.
claims.impact: When such a fetch happens while serving a request, the edge id (kept verbatim when the client supplies one) is sent to external IdPs/vendors, a behavior change those clients did not opt into and cannot turn off; correlation ids are not credentials, so harm is limited to unintended header disclosure.
claims.issue: x-request-id injection is applied unconditionally to every toolkit-http client, including third-party/external clients, with no opt-out
claims.subject: line

claims.evidence: with_request_id docs say toolkit-http requests made while serving this request carry the id; inject_request_id only warns about Buffer. REQUEST_ID is a tokio task_local, which spawned tasks do not inherit. Production handlers spawn per-request work: mini-chat stream_message wraps start_stream in tokio::spawn (messages.rs:64) and reaches the in-process OAGW facade -> proxy_request -> OAuth2 fetch_token -> RequestBuilder::send, where current_request_id() returns None and no header is sent.
claims.fix: Document the spawn limitation next to the Buffer caveat and expose a helper (e.g. `request_id_scope()` capturing current_request_id() for `with_request_id` around spawned futures), then use it in spawn-to-completion patterns that issue outbound calls.
claims.impact: For spawned request work (mini-chat streaming turns, any handler using a spawn-to-completion pattern) the downstream hop silently lacks x-request-id, so the promised edge-id correlation is inconsistent across gears; diagnostic only.
claims.issue: with_request_id promises propagation for all toolkit-http calls made while serving the request, but the task-local is silently lost across tokio::spawn and no re-scoping helper exists
claims.subject: line

claims.evidence: with_request_id uses REQUEST_ID.scope (lib.rs:281), and inject_request_id reads current_request_id() in the sending task (lib.rs:293, called from request.rs:516). Request handlers that hand work to a spawned task forward only the tracing Span, e.g. mini-chat run_to_completion `tokio::spawn(fut.instrument(tracing::Span::current()))` (messages.rs:64) and provider_task.rs:126. From there, toolkit-http sends do not carry x-request-id. Concrete path: in-process OAGW proxy_request -> OAuth2 plugin authenticate on a token-cache miss -> toolkit-auth fetch_token -> RequestBuilder::send. The doc comment says requests 'made while serving this request carry the same x-request-id' and does not mention the spawn boundary.
claims.fix: Document that the carrier does not cross tokio::spawn and that callers must re-scope it. Also provide a small helper (e.g. capture current_request_id() and wrap the spawned future in with_request_id) and use it where request work is spawned, such as mini-chat run_to_completion.
claims.impact: Precondition: a request handler issues toolkit-http calls from a spawned task, as mini-chat streaming does. Effect: those outbound calls omit x-request-id, so downstream logs cannot be correlated with the edge request. The loss is correlation/diagnostics only; no functional failure was established.
claims.issue: The x-request-id task-local carrier is silently lost across tokio::spawn, contrary to the with_request_id promise
claims.subject: line

claims.evidence: SetRequestIdLayer (gear.rs:652) keeps an inbound x-request-id and mints one only when it is absent. push_req_id_to_extensions now scopes extract_request_id(req.headers()) via with_request_id (request_id.rs:28/35), with no length or charset allowlist. RequestBuilder::send calls inject_request_id on every request whatever the destination (request.rs:516). Concrete path: OAGW proxy_handler (proxy.rs:199) -> proxy_request -> execute_auth_plugin (service.rs:697) -> OAuth2 client-credentials fetch_token on a cache miss (oauth2_client_cred_auth.rs:214) -> OIDC discovery and token POST to the external IdP, which now carry the caller-chosen id. This bypasses OAGW's upstream header passthrough policy (service.rs:661).
claims.fix: Only propagate gateway-minted ids, or validate inbound ids against a bounded allowlist (e.g. the nanoid charset, <=64 chars) and replace invalid ones before scoping. Consider limiting inject_request_id to internal/contract-client destinations.
claims.impact: Hardening only: a correlation value chosen by an external caller reaches third-party IdP/token endpoints and internal gears unbounded. It is not a credential or tenant identity, so no sensitive disclosure is established.
claims.issue: Client-supplied x-request-id is now propagated unvalidated and unbounded to every outbound toolkit-http call, including third-party hosts

claims.evidence: The mock matches only `when.method(Method::GET).path("/test")`, so it accepts a request with or without x-request-id; the test then asserts status 200 and that the mock was hit. If RequestBuilder::send (request.rs:516) minted an id outside a scope, e.g. a nanoid fallback, the test would still pass, contradicting its doc comment 'the header stays absent'. The toolkit-trace-context unit test covers inject_request_id in isolation but not the send path in request.rs.
claims.fix: Constrain the mock with `.header_missing("x-request-id")` (httpmock 0.8), so the status/`mock.assert_async()` checks fail if the header is sent.
claims.impact: A regression that makes background/startup toolkit-http calls invent request ids, polluting downstream correlation, would pass this test unnoticed.
claims.issue: test_request_id_absent_outside_scope never checks that x-request-id is absent

claims.evidence: push_req_id_to_extensions now returns `toolkit::api::with_request_id(Some(rid), next.run(req)).await`, making it the edge origin of cross-hop propagation for in-process handlers that call toolkit-http clients. Existing gateway tests (tests/request_id.rs, tests/middleware_order.rs, tests/access_log_tests.rs) assert only the XRequestId extension and the response header; none reads current_request_id() in a handler or checks an outbound toolkit-http request. Plausible wrong implementations, such as dropping the `return`, scoping only some branch, or reordering this layer outside SetRequestIdLayer so gateway-minted ids are never scoped, would pass every existing test. The OoP equivalent got such tests in oop_serve_tests.rs:697-771; the gateway did not.
claims.fix: Add a gateway test, e.g. in tests/request_id.rs, whose handler records toolkit::api::current_request_id() and asserts it equals both the supplied header and the SetRequestIdLayer-minted id when no header is sent.
claims.impact: If the edge install regresses, requests entering through the gateway and served by in-process handlers silently stop forwarding x-request-id to downstream gears via toolkit-http clients, so cross-gear log correlation, the feature this PR delivers, breaks with no failing test. Observability-only, but affects all such gateway traffic.

paid_comments.body: toolkit-http now adds x-request-id to every request, whatever the destination, and a client-supplied id is kept verbatim with no length or charset check. While the gateway serves a request, an OAGW OAuth2 client-credentials token-cache miss sends this id to the external IdP discovery and token endpoints. This bypasses OAGW's default no-passthrough header policy, and clients cannot opt out. Ids are not credentials, so this is hardening against unintended header disclosure. Fix: propagate only gateway-minted ids, or validate inbound ids (e.g. nanoid charset, at most 64 chars). Also make forwarding opt-in per client (e.g. via toolkit-contract presets), or inject the id in toolkit-contract send paths instead.

Constrain the mock with `.header_missing("x-request-id")` (httpmock 0.8), so the test fails whenever the header is sent outside a request-id scope.
